item.title: Versioned accessions make database references reproducible
item.content: A stable database accession identifies a record, while a version suffix distinguishes sequence revisions. Recording the version used in an analysis helps others recover the same sequence rather than a later revision.
item.explanationMarkdown:
For reproducibility, it is better to record the exact accession/version used in a workflow rather than only a gene name or informal label.

The general principle extends beyond sequence databases: analysis inputs should be identified precisely enough that the same input can be retrieved later.

cards.prompt: Why is recording a versioned sequence accession useful for reproducible bioinformatics?
cards.answerGuidance: Because the accession identifies the database record and the version distinguishes revisions, allowing the exact sequence used in the original analysis to be recovered.
